back: $K^{M-1}(K-1)$ for general tables: exponential in the order (Bishop 13.1).
$P\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1$ (rows sum to 1); $P^\top$ has the same eigenvalues.
Irreducible and aperiodic; some power of $P$ is strictly positive.
Unique positive $\pi$; $\mu_n\to\pi$ from any start; time averages equal $\pi$-averages.
Error $\sim|\lambda_2|^n$; spectral gap $1-|\lambda_2|$ (small gap = slow mixing).
With a symmetric proposal accept $j$ with probability $\min(1,\pi_j/\pi_i)$; the normalising constant cancels.
Independent exponential gaps with mean $1/\lambda$; count on $[0,T]$ is Poisson with mean and variance $\lambda T$.
$P(W>s+t\mid W>s)=P(W>t)$ for exponential waiting times: the continuous-time Markov property.
